post.description:
Edit an image with Ideogram 4.5 and get the result back at that image's
exact width and height. Upload the image as `image` using
`multipart/form-data`, with optional `reference_images` and a `mask`.
Returns results directly by default; set `async` or supply a
`webhook_url` to get a `generation_id` and poll
`GET /v2/generations/{generation_id}`.

Editing the whole image is bounded by 4194304 pixels (the area of a
2048x2048 square), so a larger image comes back scaled down to fit: an
8192x8192 image returns as 2048x2048.

To edit a 4K or 8K image at its full resolution, set `context_window`
to confine the edit to one region, either `auto` together with a
`mask`, or `y_min,x_min,y_max,x_max` to name the region yourself. Only
that region changes, the rest of the image comes back unchanged, and
the result keeps the image's own width and height at any input size.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.ideogram.ai/v2/image/precise-edit/ideogram-4-5 \
  -H "Api-Key: $IDEOGRAM_API_KEY" \
  -F image=@photo_8k.png \
  -F mask=@mask_8k.png \
  -F context_window=auto \
  -F prompt="Add round black sunglasses."
```

requestBody.description: A request to edit an image with Ideogram 4.5 at that image's own size. Send it as `multipart/form-data` with the `image` to edit and any `reference_images` and `mask`.

prompt.description:
The edit instruction, in natural language or as a structured JSON
prompt. Natural language is automatically converted into a
structured prompt; valid structured JSON is used as is.

image.description: The image to edit, as raw bytes (max 50MB and 67108864 pixels, which 8192x8192 meets exactly; JPEG, PNG, or WEBP). Multipart requests only, and ignored when the same image is also supplied by reference. The output always matches this image's width and height, and pixels the edit did not meaningfully change are copied exactly from it. Set `context_window` to keep the full resolution of an image over 4194304 pixels.

reference_images.description: Optional images to guide the edit (max 4, max 50MB each; JPEG, PNG, or WEBP). They are never edited themselves; only `image` is. Multipart requests only, and ignored when the same references are also supplied by reference. A request with a `mask` can include at most three, because the mask takes up one reference slot.

mask.description: An optional mask that limits the edit to part of `image` (max 50MB; JPEG, PNG, or WEBP). Multipart requests only. Black marks the area to edit and white the area to keep; values in between are rounded to the nearer of the two. The mask must have the same width and height as the image being edited and contain both black and white areas. A masked request can include at most three reference images.

context_window.description:
Which region of the image to edit. Set this to keep the full resolution of an image larger than 4194304 pixels.
`none`, the default, edits the whole image, which is bounded by 4194304 pixels (the area of a 2048x2048 square); a larger image comes back scaled down to fit. For example, an 8192x8192 image returns as 2048x2048.
`auto` requires a `mask` and fits a region around the masked area. If the mask selects more than 4194304 pixels no region fits it, and the request falls back to editing the whole image, scaled down as above.

Rows come first, matching the `bbox` ordering used elsewhere in this API, and the values are the edited image's own pixels with the origin at its top-left corner. For example `512,1024,2048,3072` is the region 2048 pixels wide and 1536 tall whose top-left corner is 1024 across and 512 down. The maximum edges are exclusive, so the region measures `x_max - x_min` by `y_max - y_min`. It must lie inside the image, measure at least 256px on each side, have an aspect ratio between 1:6 and 6:1, and cover no more than 4194304 pixels. A `mask` may select only pixels inside it.

seed.description: Random seed. Set for reproducible generation.

num_images.description: The number of images to generate.

enable_copyright_detection.description: Optional. Run copyright detection on the generated images. Adds latency; flagged images are returned with `is_image_safe: false`.

async.description: When false (the default), the request waits until the images are ready and returns them in `data`. When true, the request returns as soon as it is accepted; poll `GET /v2/generations/{generation_id}` with the returned `generation_id` for the result.

generating. The body mirrors the synchronous generate response:

containing every generated image (`url`, `prompt`, `resolution`, `seed`,

get.description:
Retrieves the current status of an asynchronous generation, and its
results once complete. Use the `generation_id` returned by any `/v2`
endpoint that runs asynchronously: every video and tool endpoint, and
any image endpoint called with `async` or a `webhook_url`.

While the generation is `pending` or has `failed`, the response
contains only `generation_id`, `status`, and `created` (plus
`failure_reason` once failed). Once `status` is `completed`, the
response includes `response_type` and `data`. Each `data` item carries
an `object_type` that identifies its shape, so image and video results
can be told apart. `usage_cost_usd_micros` reports the amount billed
when the request uses variable usage-based pricing.

Polling is rate limited per organization; a 429 response carries a
`Retry-After` header with the number of seconds to wait.

Returns your organization's invoices with their line items — the

by other members receive a 404.

200.description: The organization's invoices. Empty when no billing history exists yet.

404.description: No organization with billing access was found for this credential.

get.description:
Returns your organization's billed API usage as dense time buckets of
line items. Every line item carries the billed dollar amount; products
billed per item also carry `billed_units` (unit, quantity, and unit
price, where `quantity × unit_price = cost_total`). Usage-priced
products (billed by metered provider usage) report `cost_total` only.

Buckets cover the requested range completely — a bucket with no line
items means no billed usage in that window. Line items are unique per
bucket on (`product`, `dimensions`, `api_key.id`, unit price). Usage
billed without an API key (requests authenticated as a user session)
is included with `api_key` absent, so totals always reconcile with
your invoices.
`product` and `endpoint` are stable identifiers safe to aggregate on;
`description` is display text and may be reworded at any time.

Usage data may lag live traffic by a few minutes, and responses may be
cached briefly, so this endpoint is for reporting rather than
real-time monitoring.

Requires an API key whose owner is an organization admin. Keys owned
by other members receive a 404.

parameters.name: bucket_width
parameters.description: Bucket granularity. `1d` allows ranges up to 92 days per request; `1h` allows up to 168 hours. Page through longer histories by moving `start_time` back across successive requests.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Which billing sources to include. `api` is usage from API requests; `app` is web-app usage, attributed to the member who generated it. Defaults to both, so report totals reconcile with invoices.

200.description: Bucketed usage for the requested range.

400.description: Invalid time range, bucket width, or filters.

404.description: No organization with billing access was found for this credential.

V2ToolAdResizerPostRequestBodyContentMul.description:
The ad platform whose published safe zone the ad must stay inside.
The ad is generated inside the largest rectangle that fits the
platform's safe zone for the requested aspect ratio, and the space
around it is filled in so the output is still exactly the requested
`resolution`. `google` covers YouTube and Google Ads placements.
Use `meta_stories` or `meta_reels` for Meta placements; Reels uses
the largest rectangle inside its notched safe zone. The legacy
`meta` value is still supported and uses a more conservative safe
zone. When omitted, the ad fills the whole frame and every
supported `resolution` is accepted. Any other value is rejected
with a 400.

Each platform accepts only the resolutions for which it publishes a
safe zone; any other `resolution` is rejected with a 400:

| Platform | Accepted resolutions |
| --- | --- |
| `google` | `1920x1080`, `3840x2160`, `1080x1080`, `2400x2400`, `2880x2880`, `1080x1920`, `2160x3840` |
| `tiktok` | `1920x1080`, `3840x2160`, `1080x1080`, `2400x2400`, `2880x2880`, `1080x1920`, `2160x3840` |
| `meta_stories` | `1080x1920`, `2160x3840` |
| `meta_reels` | `1080x1920`, `2160x3840` |
| `meta` (legacy) | `1080x1920`, `2160x3840` |
| `snapchat` | `1080x1920`, `2160x3840` |
V2ToolAdResizerPostRequestBodyContentMul.title: V2ToolAdResizerPostRequestBodyContentMultipartFormDataSchemaPlatform

html_url.description:
Signed link to a self-contained HTML page displaying the editable
design, including curved text, gradients, outlines, and shadows. The
renderer, images, and fonts are embedded in the page, so it keeps
working offline once downloaded; the link itself expires after 24
hours. Uploaded `font_candidate_files` are embedded as supplied, so
redistributing the page is subject to those fonts' licenses. Empty
when the image did not pass safety checks or the page could not be
built.

The page exposes one editing API for every text layer, whether it
is drawn as HTML or on a canvas. Each layer is addressed by its
`text_blocks[].layer_id`. Scripts in the page can call
`window.layerize` (`ready`, `getTextLayers()`, `setText(id, text)`,
`update(id, patch)`, `toJSON()`, `toPNG()`); a parent page that
embeds it in an iframe sends `postMessage` requests such as
`{"type": "layerize:set-text", "id": "text-0", "text": "Hello"}`
and receives `layerize:ready`, `layerize:updated`, and
`layerize:error` replies. The page is served sandboxed with an
opaque origin, so it cannot read cookies or storage of the site
that embeds it.

A short machine-readable reason the generation failed, for example
`content_policy_violation`. Present only when `status` is `failed`.

data.description:
A list of generated images or videos. Present when `status` is
`completed`. Video entries carry an `object_type` of
`video.generation`; layerized designs carry `layerized_image`;
entries without an `object_type` are images.
